title: Овощи аль денте и куртка Кости  (Al Dente Vegetables and Kostya's Jacket)

segments.t: Behind the restaurant by the dumpsters, homeless gourmet Rodion Sergeyevich tastes the kitchen's discarded food and remarks that the vegetables are overcooked instead of true al dente. When Chef Barinov scolds Max using Rodion's exact words, Nastya asks Kostya to lend her his warm jacket to step outside.
Дошли за счет своей внутренней температуры.
Костик, отдай мне свою куртку, пожалуйста.
А что мне за это будет?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
Дошли за счет своей внутренней температуры.
'They finished cooking from their own internal heat.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'reached' and finishing on 'temperature'. Nastya answers right away.
'And some kind of stew.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'and' and 'stew' in a few short words.
'That is the cook's doing.' The meaning hinges on 'this' working together with 'cooks' in spoken Russian.
'Nastya gave it to me.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'donated' places the action in the masculine past tense. Kostya answers right away.
'Why are the two of you hanging around out here?' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'to hang around' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Go learn how to cook properly.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'go' and 'learn' in a few short words.
'A very competent person told me.' Notice how Russian expresses 'one' and 'to say' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Nastya answers right away.
'That your vegetables are supposed to be al dente.' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'dente' without extra filler words.
'Just like...' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'how' and finishing on 'by'.
'I am heading back in.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'go'. Kostya answers right away.
Костик, отдай мне свою куртку, пожалуйста.
'Kostik, lend me your jacket, please.' The meaning hinges on 'Kostik' working together with 'there you go' in spoken Russian.
'I need to step outside for a minute.' Notice how Russian expresses 'for me' and 'to marry' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
А что мне за это будет?
'And what do I get in return for that?' Kostya raises the pitch on 'will' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Now let's put it all back together and hear the whole scene again.

That wraps up this scene as in the courtyard, homeless gourmet Rodion Sergeyevich critiques Max's overcooked vegetables, and Nastya asks to borrow Kostya's warm jacket. See you next time!
